name: Hananiah (false prophet)
title: The False Prophet from Gibeon
summary: Hananiah was a false prophet from Gibeon who contradicted Jeremiah by prophesying that the yoke of Babylon would soon be broken. He broke the wooden yoke that Jeremiah wore as a symbol of Babylon's dominion, but God condemned him to death for his false prophecies.

keyEvents.title: Contradicting Jeremiah in the Temple
keyEvents.description: Hananiah prophesied in the house of the Lord that God would break the yoke of Babylon within two years and bring back the temple vessels and the exiles, including King Jeconiah.

keyEvents.title: Jeremiah's Response to the False Prophecy
keyEvents.description: Jeremiah replied that he wished Hananiah's words were true, but warned that a prophet's word must come to pass to prove they are sent by the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Breaking the Yoke from Jeremiah's Neck
keyEvents.description: Hananiah took the yoke that Jeremiah wore on his neck as a prophetic symbol and broke it in pieces before the people and the priests.

keyEvents.title: God's Judgment on Hananiah
keyEvents.description: The Lord sent Jeremiah back with a message that the wooden yoke would be replaced by an iron yoke, and that Hananiah would die within the same year because he had preached rebellion against the Lord.

keyEvents.title: The Death of Hananiah
keyEvents.description: Hananiah died in the seventh month that same year, just as Jeremiah had prophesied, as a sign that his prophecies were false.
